problems.title: Electric trainer: drag minimization at a hangar and stall corner
problems.setup: A two-seat battery electric trainer with W = 6125 N cruises at V = 50 m/s at sea level (ρ = 1.225 kg/m³). Weight and battery are fixed, so maximizing range R = η e_b (m_b/m)(L/D)/g reduces to minimizing cruise drag D(b, S) = qSC_D0 + W²/(qπeb²) with C_D0 = 0.02 and e = 0.8. Constraints: a hangar span limit b ≤ 10 m and a stall speed V_stall ≤ 25 m/s with C_Lmax = 1.6. Write g₁ = S_min − S ≤ 0, g₂ = b − 10 ≤ 0 and L = D + μ₁g₁ + μ₂g₂.

parts.ask: Before any constraints, what does each design variable want to do?
parts.a: b → ∞ and S → 0: induced drag falls as 1/b² and parasite drag falls with S, so the unconstrained problem is degenerate
w: A finite interior optimum where induced drag equals parasite drag
b → ∞ with S growing to hold the aspect ratio fixed
S → ∞ to lower the wing loading, with b → 0
sol: ∂D/∂S = qC_D0 > 0 everywhere: smaller wing, less drag
Induced equals parasite is the minimum drag speed condition, a statement about V, and V is fixed here

parts.ask: Find the cruise drag at the constrained optimum.
sol: Both constraints are active: S = S_min, b = 10 m

parts.ask: Write the KKT stationarity condition and find the span multiplier μ₂.
sol: ∇D + μ₁∇g₁ + μ₂∇g₂ = 0 with ∇g₁ = (0, −1) and ∇g₂ = (1, 0) in (b, S)
S row: qC_D0 − μ₁ = 0, so μ₁ = 30.6 N/m²
Both μ positive: the corner is a KKT point

parts.ask: How do you interpret μ₂ = 19.5 N/m for the program office?
parts.a: Shadow price: each extra metre of allowed span lowers optimal cruise drag by about 19.5 N to first order
w: Each extra metre of span raises cruise drag by about 19.5 N
The span constraint costs 19.5 N of drag in total, independent of how far it moves
A large multiplier means the constraint barely matters
sol: Exact change for b = 11 m is −16.9 N; the linear estimate is first order
Compare with the cost of folding wingtips or a wider hangar

parts.ask: What if the operator cruises at 40 m/s instead? Find the new μ₂.
sol: Signs of ∂D/∂S and ∂D/∂b are unchanged, so the same corner (b = 10 m, S = 10 m²) stays optimal
μ₂ = 2D_i/b = 30.5 N/m: span is worth more at low q, where induced drag dominates

problems.x: When each variable pushes to its bound, the optimum sits at the constraint corner, KKT confirms it with positive multipliers, and each multiplier is the shadow price of its constraint.

problems.title: Trust region step near a quartic saddle
problems.setup: f(x) = x₁⁴ − 2x₁² + x₂² has a saddle at (0, 0) and minima at (±1, 0). At x₀ = (0.5, 1) build the second-order model m(p) = f(x₀) + gᵀp + ½pᵀBp with B = ∇²f(x₀) and trust radius Δ = 1. Take the Cauchy point step. Radius rule: ρ < 0.25 shrink Δ to Δ/4 (reject if ρ ≤ 0); ρ > 0.75 with ‖p‖ = Δ double Δ; otherwise keep Δ.

parts.ask: Find g and B at x₀ and judge the pure Newton step p_N = −B⁻¹g.
parts.a: g = (−1.5, 2), B = diag(−1, 2) is indefinite, and gᵀp_N = +0.25 so p_N is an ascent direction
w: g = (−1.5, 2), B = diag(−1, 2) is indefinite, and gᵀp_N = −2.25 so p_N is a descent direction
g = (1.5, 2), B = diag(−1, 2), and gᵀp_N = −0.25 so p_N is a descent direction
g = (−1.5, 2), B = diag(2, 2) is positive definite, so Newton is safe
sol: The full step happens to land on (−1, 0): luck, with an uphill start

parts.ask: Find the Cauchy point and its predicted reduction m(0) − m(p_C).
Compute ρ = actual reduction / predicted reduction.
What happens to the iterate and the radius?
w: Accept x₁ = (1.1, 0.2) and double Δ to 2
Reject the step and shrink Δ to 0.25
Accept x₁ and shrink Δ to 0.25 because ρ < 1
sol: ρ > 0 so the step is accepted
0.25 ≤ ρ ≤ 0.75: the model is adequate, Δ stays at 1
Doubling needs ρ > 0.75 with the step on the boundary

parts.ask: What if Δ = 0.5? Find the new ρ.
sol: ρ = 0.945 > 0.75 on the boundary: accept and double Δ to 1

problems.x: A trust region minimizes a second-order model inside ‖p‖ ≤ Δ, so an indefinite Hessian is handled safely, and ρ = actual/predicted reduction decides the step and the radius.

problems.title: Drag polar surrogate: under, over and ridge
problems.setup: Wind tunnel samples on a symmetric wing give (C_L, C_D) = (0, 0.020), (0.5, 0.031), (1.0, 0.062). Fit the surrogate ŷ = w₀ + w₁C_L², which is linear in the parameters w = (w₀, w₁) with basis functions φ₀ = 1 and φ₁ = C_L². In matrix form ŷ = Φw with Φᵢⱼ = φⱼ(xᵢ), n samples and m = 2 basis functions.

parts.ask: State the fit as an optimization problem and check the dimensions.
parts.a: min over w of ‖y − Φw‖² with Φ of size n × m = 3 × 2, giving the 2 × 2 normal equations ΦᵀΦw = Φᵀy
w: Φ is m × n = 2 × 3 and w = Φ⁻¹y directly
min ‖y − Φw‖² gives ΦΦᵀw = Φᵀy, a 3 × 3 system
The model is quadratic in C_L, so it needs nonlinear least squares
sol: Error e = y − Φw, objective eᵀe = Σᵢ(yᵢ − Σⱼwⱼφⱼ(xᵢ))²
Linear in w, so the normal equations are linear even though φ₁ = C_L² is nonlinear in C_L

parts.ask: Find the induced drag factor w₁ from all three samples.
Now only the (0.5, 0.031) sample exists, so n = 1 < m = 2. Find w₁ of the minimum norm solution.
sol: One equation w₀ + 0.25w₁ = 0.031 has a line of solutions
Minimum ‖w‖² subject to Φw = y gives w = Φᵀ(ΦΦᵀ)⁻¹y
w₁ = 0.0073: the smallest weights, far from the physical K ≈ 0.04

parts.ask: Back to three samples, add ridge regularization with λ = 0.1 (penalizing both weights). Find w₁.
sol: min ‖y − Φw‖² + λ‖w‖² gives (ΦᵀΦ + λI)w = Φᵀy

parts.ask: Why does ridge also work in the n < m case?
parts.a: ΦᵀΦ + λI is m × m and positive definite for any λ > 0, so it is invertible, and as λ → 0 it tends to the minimum norm solution
w: ΦᵀΦ + λI is n × n and λ must exceed the largest eigenvalue of ΦᵀΦ
Ridge adds λ to each residual so the fit passes through every sample
Ridge needs n > m because ΦᵀΦ must already be invertible
sol: ΦᵀΦ is m × m with rank at most n < m, so it is singular
Adding λI shifts every eigenvalue up by λ > 0
λ trades fit error against weight size; pick it by cross validation

problems.x: A linear in the parameters surrogate is a least squares problem: ΦᵀΦw = Φᵀy for n > m, the minimum norm w = Φᵀ(ΦΦᵀ)⁻¹y for n < m, and ridge (ΦᵀΦ + λI)w = Φᵀy for any n.

problems.title: Armijo and curvature on a Rosenbrock slice
problems.setup: Rosenbrock f(x) = (1 − x₁)² + 100(x₂ − x₁²)² at x₀ = (0, 0) with steepest descent direction p = −∇f(x₀). Define φ(α) = f(x₀ + αp). Backtracking starts at α = 1 and halves α on each rejection. Use c₁ = 10⁻⁴ and c₂ = 0.9.

parts.ask: Find φ′(0).
Name the sufficient decrease condition and find the accepted step.
Check the curvature condition at the accepted step.
parts.a: φ′(0.125) = +9.5: the weak Wolfe condition φ′ ≥ c₂φ′(0) = −3.6 holds and strong Wolfe |φ′| ≤ 3.6 fails, so the step overshoots the minimizer of φ
w: φ′(0.125) = −9.5: both weak and strong Wolfe hold
φ′(0.125) = +9.5: weak Wolfe fails because φ′ must be negative
φ′(0.125) = +9.5: strong Wolfe holds since 9.5 ≥ −3.6
sol: Strong curvature: |9.5| ≤ 3.6, false: slope is steep and positive

parts.ask: Find the exact minimizer α* of φ.
What if c₁ = 0.5? Find the accepted step.
sol: A larger c₁ demands more decrease and gives a shorter step

problems.x: Armijo φ(α) ≤ φ(0) + c₁αφ′(0) bounds the step from above, and the strong Wolfe condition |φ′(α)| ≤ c₂|φ′(0)| keeps the step near a minimizer of φ.

problems.title: Log barrier central path in closed form
problems.setup: Minimize f = x₁² + x₂² subject to g = 2 − x₁ − x₂ ≤ 0. Each barrier subproblem minimizes B(x; μ) = f − μ ln(x₁ + x₂ − 2) for a fixed μ > 0, and μ is then reduced toward 0.

parts.ask: Find the central path point x₁(μ) for μ = 1.
At μ = 0.01, estimate the KKT multiplier from the barrier solution.
At μ = 0.01, find the optimality gap f(x(μ)) − f*.
sol: gap = 0.00999, just under the convex bound mμ = 0.01 for m = 1 constraint

parts.ask: What is μ in this method?
parts.a: A homotopy parameter held fixed within each subproblem and driven to 0 across subproblems
w: The Lagrange multiplier of g, updated by each Newton step
A penalty weight increased toward infinity
A step length chosen by line search inside each subproblem
sol: Each subproblem is an unconstrained minimization at fixed μ
Warm start the next subproblem from x(μ)
As μ → 0 the barrier Hessian grows near the boundary, so μ shrinks gradually

parts.ask: What if the constraint is x₁ + x₂ ≥ −2 instead? Estimate the multiplier at μ = 0.01.
sol: λ → 0: the unconstrained minimum (0, 0) is feasible and the constraint is inactive

problems.x: Along the log barrier central path of a convex problem, μ/(−g) converges to the KKT multiplier as μ → 0, and f(x(μ)) − f* is at most mμ for m constraints.

problems.title: Singular Hessian: valley or cliff
problems.setup: f(x) = ½xᵀHx + bᵀx with H = [[2,2],[2,2]]. Case A: b = (−4, −4). Case B: b = (−4, −2).

parts.ask: Give the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of H.
parts.a: λ = 4 along (1,1) and λ = 0 along (1,−1): positive semidefinite, axes at 45 degrees
w: λ = 2 twice: positive definite
λ = 4 along (1,−1) and λ = 0 along (1,1)
λ = 4 along (1,1) and λ = −4 along (1,−1): indefinite
sol: det H = 0, trace 4: one zero eigenvalue

parts.ask: Case A: find the minimum value of f.
sol: With s = x₁ + x₂: ½xᵀHx = s², bᵀx = −4s
f* = 4 − 8 = −4 along the whole line x₁ + x₂ = 2

parts.ask: Case A: find the distance from the origin to the closest minimizer.
Case B: evaluate f at x = (10, −10).
sol: (10, −10) lies along the null direction, so ½xᵀHx = 0
f falls by 2 per unit t along t(1,−1): unbounded below

parts.ask: Explain the test that separates Case A from Case B and sketch the contours.
parts.a: Project b onto the zero eigenvector v = (1,−1). In Case A bᵀv = 0, so b lies in the range of H, Hx = −b is solvable, contours are straight lines parallel to (1,−1), and a whole line of minimizers sits in the valley. In Case B bᵀv = −2, so f decreases linearly along v forever, contours are parabolas, and f has no minimizer.
sol: Singular H: always check the linear term

problems.x: With a singular H, the test bᵀv on the zero eigenvector v decides the case: bᵀv = 0 gives a line of minimizers and bᵀv ≠ 0 gives an unbounded function.
